x: Teaming up with Christie, Darren Braithwaite and Ade Mafe, John ran a storming 20.1 split for his leg in the 4 x 200 metres to not only beat the Americans again, but take the World Record in 1:22.11.

Round 1. 31 Aug. 18:40; heat 1 of 2; qual. first 3 + fastest 2; Temp. 30C; humidity 70%. 1, FRA 38.29; 2, GBR (T.Jarrett, J.Regis, D.Braithwaite, L.Christie) 38.36; 3, JAM 38.45. Final. 1 Sep. 16:50; temp. 28C; humidity 58%.
Lennie Paul won the 100 metres with the slight assistance of a 3 metre per second following wind to set a huge pb of 10.25, beating Olympian Darren Braithwaite by 6/100ths.
Again he beat Tokyo bound Darren Braithwaite and many of us found it hard to believe that Lennie had been passed over for the Tokyo trip in favour of slower but younger rivals.
